summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for acute abdominal pain in the epigastric and right upper quadrant, distinct from her chronic G-tube site pain and suggestive of a recurrent marginal ulcer. She had run out of oxycodone and found minimal relief with acetaminophen. An ultrasound ruled out cholecystitis, and labs showed transient leukocytosis and elevated lactate, both resolving without signs of infection. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, IV pantoprazole, and later sucralfate, with significant improvement in pain. She resumed tube feeds and oral intake, remained stable, and was discharged home with a plan to continue acid suppression and sucralfate, along with scheduled G-tube revision surgery. Discharge instructions emphasized medication adherence, avoidance of NSAIDs, and monitoring for warning symptoms.
